settings.label: Leadership coach for new managers
settings.heading: Lead your team without doing all the work
settings.text: I coach people in their first years of managing: how to delegate, give feedback, run a good meeting and keep your own work from swallowing the week.
settings.image_alt: Mateo Cruz, arms crossed, in front of a whiteboard

settings.heading: If this is your week, we should talk
settings.text: Most people are promoted for being good at the job. Nobody shows them how to lead the people doing it.

settings.title: Every question still ends up on your desk
settings.text: The team waits for you, so you answer messages until late.

settings.title: You still do the work you used to do
settings.text: It is faster to do it yourself, so you do, and your own job waits.

settings.title: Feedback you keep putting off
settings.text: One conversation you know you need to have, and it has been weeks.

settings.title: Meetings that end without a decision
settings.text: An hour a day in calls, and the same topics come back next week.

settings.title: Managing people who were your peers
settings.text: Last month you were one of them. Now you are not sure how to act.

settings.title: Your manager asks for a plan
settings.text: Goals for the team, and you are not sure where to start.

settings.heading: Three ways to work together
settings.text: Every client starts with the same free call. Then we pick what fits where you are now. Many companies pay for it from a training budget.
settings.note: Buying for several managers at your company? Ask about company rates

settings.label: One to one
settings.title: Monthly coaching
settings.text: Two calls a month and messages in between, for managers who want someone in their corner.
settings.points:
Two 60 minute calls a month
Messages answered within a working day
A one page plan we update each month
Stop or pause any month

settings.image_alt: Mateo at a whiteboard, arms crossed
settings.label: Small group
settings.title: First 90 Days
settings.text: Eight new managers, eight weeks, one topic a week: delegation, feedback, one to ones, meetings, hiring and the plan.
settings.points:
Eight live sessions on video
A workbook for each week
Two one to one calls with me
A group of managers to stay in touch with

settings.label: For your team
settings.title: Team day
settings.text: A full day with you and your team on how you work together: roles, meetings, decisions and the next quarter.
settings.points:
A call with you before the day
Six hours together, in person or online
Everything agreed, written up within a week
A follow up call after 30 days

settings.heading: From the first call to a plan you use
settings.text: No long questionnaire and no theory. We work on your real team and your real calendar from week one.
settings.image_alt: Mateo at a whiteboard, explaining with both hands

settings.title: A free call
settings.text: You tell me about your team and what is hard right now. I tell you honestly whether I can help, and how.

settings.title: Look at your week
settings.text: Where your hours go, who needs what from you and what only you can do. One page that shows it.

settings.title: Pick three changes
settings.text: Not twenty. Three habits with the most effect, each with a first step this week.

settings.title: Do the work, check in
settings.text: We meet, look at what moved and what did not, and adjust. You keep the plan between calls.

settings.heading: I learned to manage the hard way
settings.text:
I was promoted to lead a team of nine at twenty six, the week after I had been one of them. I made most of the mistakes my clients make now, usually twice.

Since then I have led teams for fourteen years and coached managers in software, retail, agencies and hospitals. The problems are almost always the same: doing too much yourself, feedback put off, and meetings that decide nothing.
settings.fact_2: Works with: Managers in their first years
settings.fact_3: Sessions: On video or in person

settings.image_alt: Mateo explaining something at a whiteboard
settings.heading: Bring it to your team or your event
settings.text: Half day and full day workshops on delegation, feedback and meetings, for leadership teams, company offsites and conferences.

settings.heading: Before you book
settings.text: Anything else? Send me a message and I will answer within a working day.

settings.question: Who do you work with?
settings.answer: People in their first few years of managing others: team leads, new heads of a function and founders hiring their first team. Most of my clients lead between three and twenty people.

settings.question: What happens on the free call?
settings.answer: Twenty minutes on video. You tell me about your team and what is hard right now, I ask a few questions, and I say honestly whether I can help. There is no pitch at the end.

settings.question: Can my company pay for it?
settings.answer: Often, yes. Many clients use a training or development budget. You get an invoice in the company's name, and I can send a short outline for your manager.

settings.question: How long do clients usually stay?
settings.answer: Most stay four to six months on monthly coaching. You can stop or pause any month, with no notice period.

settings.question: Is what I say kept private?
settings.answer: Yes. When a company pays, I share only that we are meeting, never what we talk about.

settings.question: What if it is not working?
settings.answer: Tell me. If after the first month you feel it is not worth it, I refund that month.

settings.heading: Let's look at your week
settings.text: Twenty minutes on video. You tell me about your team; I say honestly whether I can help.
settings.note: No pitch. If we are not a fit, I will say so.
settings.name: Mateo Cruz
settings.points:
Where your team is now
What is taking your time
One next step, either way
